text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing sustained apiserver 5xxs in eu-central for the past 10m. Controller-manager has restarted a few times. Suspect interaction with large GPU scale-out that started ~11:02 UTC.
leo: +1, alerts just fired. conntrack count on the NATs is near max, packets dropped.
ajay: I’m pulling logs. kube-apiserver shows lots of `dial tcp` errors to etcd peers around leader change time.
jen: GPU-autoscaler pushed 40 nodes in a short window (batch policy). Could be attaching workload + IP exhaustion.
maria: Logs snippet from one apiserver pod: ```W0507 11:06:42.123 server.go:500] apiserver proxy error: dial tcp 10.2.4.7:2379: connect: connection refused
E0507 11:06:43.456 reflector.go:201] k8s.io/...: github.com/coreos/etcd/clientv3: EOF
```
leo: NAT appliance shows conntrack entries spiking from 50k→120k in ~2m. Our conntrack limit is 128k.
ajay: Controller-manager restart trace: oomkill on reconciler worker while trying to list large number of pods right after scale event. Memory pressure + API 503s -> restart loop.
jen: Can we throttle the GPU autoscaler? We have a burst policy but no soft-splay. Recommend immediate: pause autoscaler, scale down the new attach attempts, and shift non-critical workloads to fallback region.
maria: Agreed. Leo — can you run `kubectl patch` to pause the autoscaler cron? If NAT clears we can incrementally allow attaches.
leo: Patching autoscaler now: `kubectl -n infra patch horizpodautoscaler gpu-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10}}'` (temporary). Also applying `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` on NATs while we coordinate with cloud to bump conntrack.
jen: /me will open a routing policy to divert model-serving read-only traffic to eu-west until control plane stabilizes. Small risk but reduces apiserver load.
k8s-bot: Noted: controller-manager on node pool eu-central-ctrl-2 restarted 3 times between 11:05–11:09 UTC.
ajay: I’m seeing etcd compaction sweep around the same window — disk i/o spike on leader. That plus NAT exhaustion could explain cascading failures.
maria: Plan: 1) keep autoscaler conservative 2) bump conntrack temporarily 3) divert non-essential traffic to fallback region 4) investigate compaction schedule and add jitter to autoscaler bursts.
leo: Already asked infra to increase NAT conntrack and check for firmware bug. Cloud support ticket created: #INC-5429.
jen: Also adding a quick alert to detect >80% conntrack and apiserver 5xx correlation so we can auto-throttle next time.
ajay: For postmortem — capture: compaction timing, autoscaler burst policy, controller-manager memory headroom, and NAT conntrack headroom. Risk/cost tradeoff: increasing conntrack capacity reduces failures but adds cost; prefer autoscaler smoothing.
maria: Thanks — I’ll keep this thread updated. If we see apiserver 503s drop below 1% in 15m we can slowly reopen attach window. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary traffic adjusted: routed 30% model-serving reads to eu-west at 11:12 UTC per request.
leo: Current metrics: conntrack 95k -> 78k after scaling back attaches, apiserver 5xxs reduced to ~0.8% in last 4m. Continuing to monitor.
jen: Filing follow-up runbook changes and autoscaler config PR after this incident.
maria: Closing action items in the ticket and will draft a short postmortem once we have logs aggregated. Thanks everyone.
